command: cd <sandbox-ws> && DSH_HOME=<sandbox>/home HOME=<sandbox>/userhome DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT=<sandbox>/ws dsh --profile w --patch <sandbox>/cellwork-overlay.yml --port 3299 --no-open

profile.shape: sandbox profile w: dsh.profile.bundles = [@deepseek-ai/dsh-base, @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app, @mpd-dsh/mpd]; node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd symlinked to the checkout; dependencies.@mpd-dsh/mpd = link:<checkout>

overlay.why: On this machine the bundle resolution picks a STALE @mpd-dsh/mpd (0.15.5, no cellwork row) even when the profile links the checkout, so the row was supplied through a --patch overlay with an ABSOLUTE module path. This proves the row MODULE applies; it does not prove the bundle patch is the source.

observed.loaderFailures: none observed (no 'failed to apply loader entry' / 'failed to load' line)

proves: The row's apply() ran to completion under a REAL dsh boot in an isolated DSH_HOME/HOME/workspace (not --dump-config).

The mount line is written at the END of apply(), after the guard install and the three registerTool calls and the cellwork command registration, with the config it resolved (guard=on, depthMax=3, checkpointRatio=0.5, windowFraction=0.25, no override).
The boot's composed tree contained the row at the absolute module path (dump-config excerpt).
doesNotProve: That the bundle's own cordis.patch.yml row is the source of that mount — an overlay row was used because the local bundle resolution is stale. The bundle wiring is proven separately by verify:rows (37 ids incl mpd-cellwork) and verify:manifest (row module paths resolve).
The `dsh plugin add` install/uninstall path (needs the registry; bundle-lifecycle dies at install on this network — recorded bound).
A session-level tool LIST (a request/header tools[] witness for cellwork_status/cellwork_start/cellwork_stop); the unit suite proves the registrations, this boot proves apply.
